answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it can place orders, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove collusion through signed, conflicting commitments. One operator can still create many identities, but each needs separately funded collateral and ties up capital; detected Sybils lose it. A tundra market may see a small ripple in prices, while yarrow trades remain open to newcomers once they post the same bond.
